newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel plans more investment aid for settlements.
newsitem.headline: Israel plans more investment aid for settlements.

text.p: Israeli Finance Minister Dan Meridor has asked the parliamentary finance committee to approve loans guarantees for factories built in West Bank and Gaza settlements, the Treasury said on Sunday.
The proposal is part of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's effort to encourage Israeli investment in the West Bank by renewing government-financed incentives.

Under the proposal, the government will guarantee up to 85 percent of a loan taken out for an "approved enterprise" for up to 30 percent of the total unmortgaged assets. The aid will be granted retroactive to August 2, 1996.
The Treasury is seeking permission to provide 25.5 million shekels in guarantees for 1997, which would facilitate investments of up to 100 million shekels.

The previous Labour government ended subsidies over Israel's pre-1967 border, often called the Green Line, in 1992. Treasury officials said the political risk of investing in the West Bank has stopped Israeli banks from lending there.

"The...(loan-guarantees) decision was taken because of the difficulties in obtaining bank loans against land and buildings that are part of the projects, as a result of which investors over the Green Line are discriminated against vis a vis investors elsewhere," the Treasury said in a statement.

Israel has already handed major urban centres in the West Bank to Palestinian control and is due to make further withdrawals by mid-1998. The two sides are also due to begin talks on the final status of the region.

The government voted to renew investment incentives for factories in the West Bank and Gaza on August 2, but as part of an overall reform of the Law for Encouragement of Investments had done away with state loan guarantees for approved investments.
The guarantees now will apply only to West Bank and Gaza settlements.
Like other government-designated development zones, enterprises in the territories are also entitled to grants of up to 24 percent of the total investments and tax relief.
